title: System Design for Web Apps
description: Design large-scale distributed systems. Load balancing, caching, CDN, microservices, message queues, and event-driven architecture.

topics.title: Horizontal vs Vertical Scaling
topics.content:
### When One Server Isn't Enough

#### Vertical Scaling (Scale Up)
Upgrade the single server's hardware: more RAM, faster CPU, bigger disk.

- ✅ Simple — no code changes needed
- ✅ No distributed systems complexity
- ❌ Has a hard limit (biggest server available)
- ❌ Single point of failure
- ❌ Expensive at the high end

#### Horizontal Scaling (Scale Out)
Add more servers and distribute traffic between them.

- ✅ Theoretically unlimited scale
- ✅ Fault tolerant (one server dies, others continue)
- ✅ Cheaper at scale (commodity hardware)
- ❌ Requires stateless application design
- ❌ Distributed systems complexity (consistency, coordination)

```
              ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
  Clients     │         Load Balancer            │
  ───────►    │  (nginx, AWS ALB, Cloudflare)    │
              └───────┬─────────┬───────┬───────┘
                      │         │       │
                 ┌────▼──┐ ┌───▼──┐ ┌──▼────┐
                 │ App 1 │ │ App 2│ │ App 3 │
                 └────┬──┘ └───┬──┘ └──┬────┘
                      └────────┴───────┘
                               │
                    ┌──────────▼──────────┐
                    │  Shared Database     │
                    └─────────────────────┘
```

**Key requirement for horizontal scaling**: Your app must be **stateless**. No user sessions stored in memory — use Redis or a database.

Microservices vs Monolith
topics.content:
### Choosing Your Architecture

#### The Monolith

One deployable unit. All features in the same codebase.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│           MONOLITH                   │
│  ┌──────────┐  ┌──────────────────┐ │
│  │   Auth   │  │    Products      │ │
│  └──────────┘  └──────────────────┘ │
│  ┌──────────┐  ┌──────────────────┐ │
│  │  Orders  │  │   Notifications  │ │
│  └──────────┘  └──────────────────┘ │
└──────────────────┬──────────────────┘
                   │
              Single DB
```

✅ Simple to develop and deploy  
✅ Easy debugging  
✅ No network latency between modules  
❌ Entire app redeploys on any change  
❌ Can't scale individual components  

#### Microservices

Each service is independently deployed and has its own database.

```
  ┌──────────┐   ┌──────────┐   ┌──────────┐
  │   Auth   │   │ Products │   │  Orders  │
  │  Service │   │ Service  │   │ Service  │
  └────┬─────┘   └────┬─────┘   └────┬─────┘
       │              │               │
  ┌────▼─────┐  ┌────▼─────┐  ┌─────▼─────┐
  │ Auth DB  │  │ Prod DB  │  │ Orders DB │
  └──────────┘  └──────────┘  └───────────┘
```

✅ Each service scales independently  
✅ Teams can deploy independently  
✅ Failure isolation  
❌ Complex distributed system  
❌ Network latency between services  
❌ Much harder to debug

**Rule**: Start with a monolith. Extract microservices only when you have a specific scaling reason and a team large enough to own each service.
